title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated images and videos of a real, named attorney were used to create fake social media profiles and solicit payment for immigration services he never offered. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI deployment but in the deliberate misuse of AI tools by outside actors to manufacture convincing false identities at scale. The volume reported, nearly 6,500 fake profiles removed across multiple platforms, shows that automated content generation allowed the scheme to propagate far faster than manual impersonation could have.

The point where detection was possible was at the platform level, where content-moderation systems did not flag or remove the fake profiles until an external anti-piracy firm was retained to do so. Social media platforms' own systems apparently did not catch the coordinated inauthentic behavior, the repeated use of a single real person's likeness, or the pattern of accounts directing users off-platform to payment apps. The gap between creation and removal allowed real financial harm to occur, including at least one reported case of a victim losing thousands of dollars.

What is not established is who conducted the fraud, where it originated, or whether any platform violated a legal duty by failing to act sooner, as no investigation findings or legal rulings are reported.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of criminals using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provides, including US residency assistance for $2,200. The fraud escalated dramatically over the past three months, with criminals directing victims through social media to WhatsApp, where they send phony contracts and request payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App.

After learning about the scheme from incoming client calls, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scam's origin. He advises immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be wary of social media advertisements demanding immediate payment, noting that his office never requests payments over the phone.
